paper.abstract_en: This dissertation investigates dark matter on both cosmological and local scales. On large scales, the cross-correlation between weak gravitational lensing from the Kilo-Degree Survey (KiDS) and the unresolved gamma-ray background measured by the Fermi Large Area Telescope is analysed. No statistically significant correlation is detected, allowing upper limits to be placed on dark matter annihilation and decay scenarios. On small scales, the detection efficiency of ultra-faint dwarf galaxies is quantified using image-level injection–recovery simulations. The results improve our understanding of survey selection functions and the incompleteness of satellite galaxy catalogues. Together, these studies provide complementary constraints on dark matter models and establish a basis for future investigations with next-generation survey data.
